newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks up but off record high.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks up but off record high.

text.p: Jakarta stocks closed higher on Tuesday but off the record touched earlier in the day on active buying of blue chips and secondaries, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index closed up 7.06 points, or 0.97 percent, at 731.62 points after touching a record 732.52. Gainers led losers by 79 to 52, with 72 counters unchanged. Total turnover was about 659 billion rupiah.
"Today's rise in the index was the result of a strong rebound in Sampoerna and sustained buying interest in Telkom," a broker with PT Vickers Ballas Tamara said.
"But large profit taking in some medium-sized stocks such as Bukaka and Bakrieland pulled the index back slightly," he said.

Share prices of Bukaka and Bakrieland had risen sharply in active trading in the past week on market talk of a possible rights issue and dividend of Bukaka and possible involvement of Bakrieland in a mass rapid transportation project, brokers said.
The Vickers broker predicted the potential upside for the index on Wednesday was small as many investors, particularly local players, were likely to take their profits in some secondaries.
Brokers and analysts said the sharp rebound in cigarette maker Sampoerna had boosted sentiment on firstliners.
Blue chip such as Bank Negara Indonesia, Semen Gresik, Indosat and Bimantara Citra were also targetted by buyers, brokers said.
Sampoerna was up 5.39 percent, to close at 9,775 rupiah on active turn-over of 2.9 million shares, while Telkom was last traded at 4,075 rupiah, 100 rupiah higher on a volume of 2.8 million shares.
Mooto Murata, senior analyst at Daiwa Research Institute in Jakarta, said some blue chips were still trading below 20 times 1997 projected earnings.
He said Indonesia' strong economic fundamentals combined with relatively cheap blue chip stocks had attracted foreign buyers into the Jakarta market.
